newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES rises on key shareholder rule, market firmer.
newsitem.headline: UES rises on key shareholder rule, market firmer.

text.p: News Russia's biggest company UES scrapped restrictions on individual investor shareholdings boosted share prices in late afternoon trade but failed to lure Western investors back to the "blue chip" fold, dealers said.
The Russian Trading System of 22 leading shares closed at 355.64 after 353.41 on Thursday on total market volume of $36.7 million.
Dealers forecast the market would remain quiet through next week.

"The market needs foreign currency buying orders (to grow)," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Alexander Zyuzlikov, saying he had seen mostly rouble deals on Friday. "When currency deals appear we'll be able to say that the West has woken up."
Traders say many investors have transferred funds into the less liquid and undervalued second and third tier stocks.
UES EESR.RTS shareholders voted to promote vice-president Boris Brevnov to chief executive, and overturned rules limiting individual holdings to one percent of voting shares.
"Russian players took the opportunity to drive it up, and it rose very well," said Zyuzlikov, adding UES pulled several leading stocks up with it.
UES rose to $0.3179 at the end of trading from Thursday's closing $0.3115 while natural gas producer Gazprom GAZP.RTS recovered slightly from losses on Thursday, rising to $0.635 from $0.605.

National savings bank Sberbank SBER.RTS rose to $142.50 from $139.50 on news it would pay a 30,000 rouble dividend on ordinary shares with a face value of 50,000 roubles on 1996 results, traders said.
But oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS slipped to $14.94 from $14.95 and long-distance provider Rostelekom RTKM.RTS edged down to $3.780 from $3.850.
But traders said the market would stay range-bound over most of June as liquidity dried up.
"Right now only corporate news is going to influence the mrarket in particular stocks," said Regent European Securities head of trading Dmitry Starenko.
"I don't expect the market to go up or down significantly in the next couple of weeks -- summer is coming up."
